findings.title: Native pre-capture resource failure still forgets handed spend after owner mapping replacement and permits duplicate dispatch
findings.smallest_reproduction: probe_native.py run(994) under recorded CPython3.12.3/default recursion limit1000: create ordinary synthetic battery desk, dispatch once and settle charge, call reader.pinned through deep recursion, catch native RecursionError, replace owner mapping ledger with saved pre-spend BudgetLedger checkpoint, dispatch original admitted action again. Adjacent depth995 reproduces; depth993 refuses.
findings.actual_result: At depth994 and995 _uncompared retains raw tuple referencing live owner mappings; _unread_entries empty. After replacement redispatch_refused=false and calls=2. No monkeypatch, private reader state mutation, signals, timing race, or forged owner involved. All printed state is observation only.
findings.expected_result: A returned spend-bearing handing cannot disappear before authoritative comparison and restore the original action currentness; retry must recover handed spend or remain transiently refused without permanently poisoning honest readers.
findings.in_process_trust_scope: Within documented in-process handoff boundary: exact native BudgetLedger, ordinary execution-side settlement and checkpoint replacement. Not execution-private introspection/mutation, not an entirely between-verifications unobserved spend. The tuple was demonstrably returned and retained before owner replacement.
findings.proposed_correction: Choose and specify execution-side handing lifetime/publication semantics that preserve mapping bindings until reader retention/comparison. Concrete bounded option: each callback publishes new native dict snapshots and never mutates those published dictionaries; owner checkpoint replacements affect only current owner dictionaries. Matched fresh-dict control refuses the identical depths994/995. Retain existing owner classes/history normalization, no parallel budget state. Decide account/entry lifetime rules explicitly for any supported non-monotonic owner mutation. Do not declare generic acknowledgement mandatory solely from this experiment.

correction_assessment.json_parity: Locally corrected. _retained_entry uses BudgetCharge.from_dict before ledger sorted JSON/default=str and final from_dict, versus ScientificEvaluation JSON before readback plus writability for experiment. R16/R17 32 controls and eight independent composite transitions pass. No new serializer widening or false detached divergence established.
correction_assessment.doc_correction: owners.py449-456 explicitly treats pre-capture loss as unresolved defect; old caller-stack exclusion removed from current class contract.
correction_assessment.owner_decision: A precise publication lifetime decision remains necessary if current callbacks may return mutable live maps. Experiment demonstrates a simple owner-side fresh-dict publication control; does not establish a need for generalized reservation, persistent journal, or acknowledgement subsystem.
correction_assessment.generic_local_alternatives: Additional local retries/copies reduce failure windows but can themselves be interrupted before stable retention. Permanent retirement from interruption alone violates honest-reader recovery invariant. Blind retry against current mutable map loses history as reproduced. Durable at-most-once at desk is a different explicitly absent contract. A fresh-thread approach might mitigate bounded recursion but is not demonstrated sufficient against repeated interruption/allocation failure or caller-held-lock lifetime and would require its own bounded review.
correction_assessment.lifetime_detail: For shown native-ledger checkpoint replacement, retaining a fresh binding snapshot keeps original append-only ledger reachable even when active mapping changes; full owner checkpoint cloning or acknowledgement is not needed by this reproduction. A broader publication contract must state whether nested entry payload mutation is in trusted execution-private scope, rather than claim graph immutability from shallow dict copying.
